analyzed_vuln.description: IPv6Layer::parseExtensions() constructs extension objects based only on `offset <= m_DataLen - 2` and then unconditionally reads extension header fields via `newExt->getExtensionLen()` / `getBaseHeader()->nextHeader` without verifying that the extension header bytes are actually within bounds. For malformed/truncated packets, `offset` can point near the end of the buffer; `IPv6Extension::getExtensionLen()` then dereferences `getBaseHeader()->headerLen` out of bounds, causing the ASan heap-buffer-overflow. Root cause is missing per-extension length/bounds validation in parseExtensions before accessing extension header bytes.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: FuzzTarget feeds a crafted pcap packet parsed through NflogLayer as IPv6 payload. Input must satisfy minimal IPv6 validity to reach `IPv6Layer::parseExtensions()`, with `nextHeader` indicating an extension type (e.g., fragment/hop-by-hop/etc.) while actual payload is truncated so extension base header is not fully present at computed `offset`. parseExtensions still instantiates an extension and calls getExtensionLen()/getBaseHeader(), leading to OOB read.
